The Gators, led by third-year head coach [[Todd Golden]], played their home games at the [[O'Connell Center]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]], as members of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). During this season, Florida experienced its most success in 11 years and restored itself as an elite program. Paying homage to the Florida team that won back-to-back championships 18 years prior, this team adopted the motto, "'''Gator Boys Stay Hot'''". Led by senior guards [[Walter Clayton Jr.]], [[Will Richard]], and [[Alijah Martin]], Florida posted a 27–4 regular season record, finishing second in the most difficult SEC season in conference history. The Gators got off to a hot start when they finished non-conference play with a 13–0 record and No. 6 ranking in the AP Poll, which was their highest ranking in 7 years. Despite early losses to [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] and [[2024–25 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]], Florida got hot and finished the regular season winning 9 of their last 10 games. During this stretch, they pulled off massive wins on the road against [[2024–25 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|No. 1 Auburn]] and [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|No. 7 Alabama]]. Led by Clayton Jr. and [[Alex Condon]], Florida was able to beat a No. 1 team on the road for the first time in program history. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] at [[Bridgestone Arena]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]], they defeated [[2024–25 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]], 95–81, in the quarterfinals and [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], 104–82, in the semifinals to advance to the SEC Championship, where they defeated [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], 86–77, to clinch their first SEC championship since [[2013–14 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2014]]. They received an automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#West regional – San Francisco, California|West region]]. They defeated [[2024–25 Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball team|Norfolk State]], 95–69, in the first round, [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|two-time]] [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|defending national champions]] [[2024–25 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], 77–75, in the second round, and [[2024–25 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]], 87–71, in the Sweet Sixteen to advance to the Elite Eight. There, they defeated [[2024–25 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]], 84–79, to advance to their first Final Four since 2014. They would then defeat SEC rival Auburn, 79–73, to advance to their first [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship]] since 2007.{{cite web |last=Salerno |first=Cameron |last2=Cobb |first2=David |date=2025-04-06 |title=Florida back in NCAA title game for first time since 2007 after wild comeback win vs. Auburn in Final Four |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/florida-back-in-ncaa-title-game-for-first-time-since-2007-after-wild-comeback-win-vs-auburn-in-final-four/live/ |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=CBS Sports}} In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]], they overcame a 12-point deficit late in the second half to beat [[2024–25 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]], 65–63, to clinch their third national title overall and their first since [[2006–07 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2007]].{{Cite web |last=Pells |first=Eddie |date=2025-04-07 |title=Walter Clayton Jr.'s defensive stop gives Florida its 3rd national title with 65-63 win over Houston |url=https://apnews.com/article/march-madness-florida-houston-ncaa-championship-74a9c790277595ce53ca130c5ec64429 |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=[[Associated Press]] |language=en}} ==Previous season== The [[2023–24 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Gators]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 24–12, 11–7 in SEC play, to finish in sixth place. In the [[2024 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], the Gators beat [[2023–24 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], 85–80, in the first round, [[2023–24 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], 102–88, in the second round, and [[2023–24 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]], 95–90, in the semifinals to advance to the championship game where they would fall to [[2023–24 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]], 86–67.
